statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at 15 of 100 in the low band, ten points below the 25 block threshold, while stress remains extreme at 86 and confidence is high at 88.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold and the deterministic mapping therefore returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The named danger window covers the August CPI release at 12:30 UTC on 11 September and the first cash-open hour that follows, where the conditional path peaks at WATCH.
headline: The 22:00 UTC CME reopen resolves the Oracle checkpoint without a gap: NQ trades 29,148.50, up 0.05%, in a 22-point band on roughly 1,200 contracts, and tail eases from 18 to 15 while a 4.944% ten-year and Brent at $109.02 hold stress at 86.
body:
The checkpoint named in the previous assessment has now been observed, and it resolved benignly. CME equity futures reopened from the daily maintenance halt at 22:00 UTC. In the first twenty minutes NQ traded 29,148.50, up 0.05% against the 29,135.25 pause reference, inside a band of 29,134.50 to 29,156.75 on roughly 1,200 contracts. That is a 22-point range with no gap and no directional leg. The prior hour carried tail at 18 precisely because a large single-stock earnings impulse was about to meet the index in thin post-close liquidity with an unknown transmission. The transmission has now been measured and it is negligible, so the step is given back and tail moves to 15.

The single-name picture supports that reading rather than complicating it. Oracle published fiscal first-quarter results at 20:10 UTC: total revenue of $19.3 billion, up 30%, total cloud revenue of $11.6 billion, up 62%, cloud infrastructure revenue of $7.4 billion, up 121%, non-GAAP earnings of $1.92 per share, and remaining performance obligations of $664 billion, an increase of $209 billion year over year. The company delivered more than 300,000 GPUs to AI cloud customers during the quarter and disclosed a completed $20 billion at-the-market common stock sale. Fiscal 2027 guidance was set at a minimum of $90 billion in revenue and $8.10 in non-GAAP earnings per share, with second-quarter revenue growth guided to 30% to 34%. Against a regular session that closed down 5.38% at $152.94, the shares were quoted at $159.41 shortly after 22:00 UTC, up 4.23%. That is a fade from the roughly 7% gain quoted an hour earlier, while the conference call is still under way. An after-hours impulse that gives ground rather than extends is mean-reverting behaviour, and it is the opposite of the path this framework treats as dangerous.

The index structure behind it is unchanged. Cash NAS100 closed at 29,103.51, down 318.04 points or 1.08%, with the whole session contained inside a 212-point band between 29,038.22 and 29,250.41. The opening-auction low was set in the first hour and never revisited, and the path offered retracement in both directions throughout. The broader tape closed lower for a fourth consecutive session, with the S&P 500 down 0.58% at 7,591.70 and the Dow down 316.56 points at 52,064.10. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach, not the size of a decline, and nothing in Thursday's path or in tonight's reopen fits that description.

What keeps stress in the extreme band is the macro and cross-asset backdrop, which if anything firmed into the close. The ten-year Treasury yield settled at 4.944%, up 10.7 basis points and near the top of a 4.879 to 4.952 range, its highest since 2023. The two-year is at 4.586%, a 52-week high, and the thirty-year reached about 5.35%, the highest since 2007. That is a bear steepening of the whole curve, confirmed by Treasury futures weakening progressively out the curve. Crude extended sharply, with WTI quoted at $103.98, up 6.69%, and Brent at $109.02, up 6.34%, after settlements of $102.48 and $107.63, the highest closes since 19 May. The driver is an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict in which Saudi output has fallen to its lowest since 1990 and Iran has signalled an exclusion zone near the Strait of Hormuz. VIX closed at 17.84, up more than 8% and at the top of its 16.29 to 18.17 range. Gold fell 1.2% on the day, which points to a real-rate and energy repricing rather than a broad flight to safety. August producer prices, published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics at 12:30 UTC, rose 0.4% month over month and 5.4% year over year, with final demand goods up 1.1% on a 4.2% energy increase and diesel up 24.1%. Latest-session sector context showed semiconductors weaker than the broader index.

The forward window is shaped by one scheduled event. The August consumer price report is released at 12:30 UTC on 11 September, confirmed against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedule, and it is the last inflation reading before the FOMC decision on 16 September. Conditional tail peaks at 23 in that slot and holds 23 at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the cash open, then eases to 20 at the University of Michigan release. All three map to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold of 25, because no post-release price path is observed at publication time and, under this framework, surprise magnitude and forecast dispersion widen uncertainty before they raise tail. What would raise tail is observable rather than hypothetical: an opening auction that extends without meaningful retracement, repeated extension after failed pullbacks, or price holding near session extremes. None of that is in evidence tonight.

Confidence rises to 88. The single limitation of the previous hour, the absence of a live price path during the maintenance halt, has been removed by the reopen, and current verified levels are in hand across the index, futures, the two-year and ten-year, crude, volatility, the published producer price data, the Oracle actuals and the confirmed release calendar. The remaining caveats are narrow and stated: the futures sample is only about twenty minutes long and thin, and Oracle's call has not yet produced published commentary.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 22:00 UTC on 9 September to 21:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 9 and holds a tight 8 to 11 band through the U.S. overnight, the Asian session and the European morning, with the dominant mode recorded as mixed throughout. The regime change sits in the middle of the U.S. session: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode turned trend-down on the pre-release grind, 20 at 12:00 UTC when the August producer price report printed and the mode became event/whipsaw, and a 24 peak at 13:00 UTC covering post-release discovery and the cash open. Those two slots are the only ones in the window that mapped to WATCH. The final eight slots record the decay back into range and then a modest rebuild: 17, 14, then 16 as yields and crude extended, 15, 16, 17 into the final cash hour, 19 at 20:00 UTC as Oracle's results landed after the close, and 18 at 21:00 UTC across the CME maintenance halt. Stress never left the extreme band, running 80 to 87 throughout. That is the defining feature of the window: a persistently difficult environment in which the observed price path nevertheless kept offering retracement.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the observed 22:00 UTC reopen on 10 September and ends in the New York afternoon of 11 September. Conditional tail starts at 15, the level the resolved Oracle checkpoint supports, and holds there through the conference-call hour before easing to 14 as Tokyo opens. It decays through 13 and settles at a 12 floor across the thinnest Asian and pre-European hours, where no U.S. macro is scheduled. From the European pre-market it rebuilds gradually, 13 through 14, and reaches 16 in the final full hour before the release. The window peak is 23 in the 12:00 UTC slot containing the August consumer price report and 23 again at 13:00 UTC where post-release discovery overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open, then 20 at the University of Michigan release; all three map to WATCH and none reaches the block threshold, since no post-release price path is observed. The path then eases to 17, 15, 14 and 14 through the New York afternoon before ticking to 15 and 16 into the weekly close, as pre-weekend adjustment concentrates into a week that has closed lower four sessions running with an unresolved Persian Gulf conflict carrying across the weekend, and settles at 15 in the 21:00 UTC maintenance halt. Stress stays in the extreme band throughout, peaking at 90 around the release, and confidence declines from 88 to 60 with distance from observed evidence.
